fallback_items_done.note: ASSESSED AND NOT DONE, with the reason recorded. Converting a working read path to code that cannot be run, in the same commit as a security fix, is the inverse of the argument that makes the new Drizzle adapters safe to leave unexecuted. billing-enrichment.ts is the tractable one and is recorded as owed.

fallback_items_done.title: the flat-fee scenarios
fallback_items_done.note: 34 scenarios plus a coverage map: 24 covered, 10 gaps. Eight of the ten are one gap - the SQL has never run. Gap 1 was closed while writing the map.

fallback_items_done.title: the ocpp_identities retirement plan
fallback_items_done.note: 64 readers in four tiers; only the auth path can take the site down. Two findings: the Durable Object keys on ocpp_identities.id, so the backfill must carry ids across or every live DO is orphaned at cutover; and an identity ever CHANGED in place cannot be reconstructed - a permanent hole, recorded rather than papered over.

fallback_items_done.title: the createCharger call-site migration
fallback_items_done.note: done inside the asset-model retirement plan, both callers named with the ordering constraint.

fallback_items_done.title: lifetime-counter maintenance
fallback_items_done.note: store the reading, never accumulate. Assignment with a guard: replay is a no-op, out-of-order is a no-op, a backwards reading is REFUSED and what to do then is deliberately left open so the event is visible first.

fallback_items_done.title: the OCPI mapping note
fallback_items_done.note: EVSE.uid is the placement, never the device. The move maps onto moveDevice and the wire order matters. The status conversion is lossy and is written out.

fallback_items_done.title: what now stands between here and a real invoice
fallback_items_done.note: LONGER than round 3, and that is honest: round 3 counted what stood between the code and AN invoice; round 4 made it correct and correctness added items that were always there.

backlog_items_done.note: zaptec-session-sync.ts:235 priced a CDR with no Energy at zero AND marked it complete on Zaptec-native installations, because no OCPP row existed to disagree. Now skipped by name. Census: one storing coalesce fixed, nine displaying ones recorded as not the same defect.

backlog_items_done.title: Charger.Active consumers
backlog_items_done.note: the field is already read and dropped by zaptec-charger-status-sync, which persists its two neighbours. 11 read paths censused: 5 matter, 2 matter in the OPPOSITE direction, 4 do not. Three rules, and the ordering - writer, backfill, filters - must not overlap.

backlog_items_done.title: property-based tests for the temporal key
backlog_items_done.note: 5 tests over 8 seeds, deterministic PRNG, no new dependency. Both directions: accepted sets hold the invariant, and every rejection genuinely collides. The ADR claim about the partial index is generated rather than worked once.

The PostgreSQL version Neon serves is unrecorded. Migrations 0005 and 0006 ship both constraint forms so this does not block, but it must be answered before either is applied.
Mid-month proration is Andri's commercial decision. Both branches are implemented; the default is today's behaviour so nothing changes silently.
The accountant's constraint on invoice numbering is still unanswered. Three things it could move are each a one-place change by construction.
Five Dalvegur chargers exist in the Zaptec portal with no row in our database. No predicate can see them; it under-bills and needs a reconciliation.

very_tldr: Six phases, six commits, five migrations generated and none applied. The invoice sequence is now gap-free and unique; devices, identities and placements are effective-dated with the temporal key emitted in both PostgreSQL forms; the ADR's double-invoice is a named test that proves the constraint refuses it and the rejected partial index permits it. Billing now counts placement overlap rather than current rows, which is the fix for a mid-month move billing the wrong host - and for Dalvegur it takes the connector count from 30 to 20. Three of B's schema requests answered, two serviced and one refused for creating a cross-tenant idempotency namespace. Two real defects found while writing the dry run: a dropped sequence state that was indistinguishable from correct output, and proration losing an eyrir per move.
